## Context

The first attempt at replacing the edge-triggered Jira bridges (epic 3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f, now superseded) shipped the operational infrastructure successfully: legacy bridge YAMLs deleted from main, reconcile-bridge.yml workflow plus heartbeat canary plus weekly fsck audit live, ACLI integration hardened with 36 contract tests verifying 21 of 22 invocation patterns against authoritative Atlassian docs. Pass-1 live verification against the live DIG Jira project then surfaced an architectural defect: the snapshot-diff differ emitted create mutations without a direction marker, and the applier dispatched every create to client.create_issue() — creating duplicate Jira issues instead of mirroring unmapped Jira issues down as local jira-* tickets. The defect was compounded by bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json writes being lost between GHA runs because the workflow only committed the tickets-tracker dir, so every pass started with an empty prior-snapshot and emitted create for every Jira issue. Five duplicate Jira issues were created before the pass was halted; the JQL-label dedup short-circuit prevented approximately 1,820 more.

EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

This epic delivers the redesigned reconciler: derivable rather than snapshot-diff, with direction-tagged mutations that make the inversion bug structurally impossible at the type level. The design absorbed empirical findings from a live spike against current DIG state (direction safety operator gate PASSED; 197 stale-label bridge orphans identified as residue of the prior failed pass), a focused pre-mortem dispatch (found a real next-class defect — dedup-JQL fossilization of failed-rollback orphans — and proposed a 3-layer fix that is folded into this design), an architectural probe spec at docs/integration-harness-jira-reconciler-derivable.md, and a 84-ticket cruft cleanup of local state (4 telemetry bugs plus 80 PR-comment-deferred placeholders) that brought the day-one bootstrap working set to approximately 931 mutations across 388 outbound creates plus 346 inbound creates plus 197 inbound label-strips. Local state after that cleanup is accepted as source of truth for what Jira should mirror after migration.

Operator-trust signals are preserved from the prior epic: every reconciler pass produces either zero anomalies or an actionable bug ticket per anomaly class. Project maintainers and future DSO operators on Jira-mirrored projects need this convergent sync as platform-level infrastructure (currently single-project usage).

## Approach

Derivable reconciler topology. Single pass orchestrator (reconcile.py) loads local state via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list` (index, no per-ticket replay) and Jira state via scoped ACLI search, then calls a pure differ that returns a flat list of direction-tagged mutations, then dispatches via a narrow applier matrix. Stateless: two passes on identical (local, jira) inputs produce byte-identical mutation lists. No bridge_state/ persistence. No mapping.json source-of-truth.

Differ contract (differ.py). compute_mutations(local_state, jira_state) returns list[Mutation]. Each Mutation carries direction (inbound | outbound) and action (create | update | delete | probe | clean_label | repair_property). Direction is computed from source:
- Jira issue with no dso-id label and no matching dso_local_id entity property: (inbound, create) — mirror down as jira-<key> local ticket with all fields mapped from Jira plus the audit tag imported:reconciler-bootstrap
- Local ticket with no jira-* prefix and no Jira twin claiming its identity: (outbound, create) — push to Jira with mandatory dual identity write (label plus entity property)
- Both sides exist with field divergence: conflict_resolver chooses direction; local-wins on scalars produces outbound, additive merge on collections produces inbound
- Both sides exist with one side closed: close propagates per local-wins to outbound_delete (Jira close, not hard delete)
- Jira issue carries dso-id:<L> label but local has no ticket with id L AND no current jira-* mirror references the Jira key: (inbound, clean_label) — strip stale dso-id label; next pass mirrors normally as fresh jira-<key>. Addresses the 197 visible bridge orphans, residue of the prior failed reconciler pass.
- Jira issue carries dso-id:<L> label matching an active local L but is missing the dso_local_id entity property: (inbound, repair_property) — retry-wrapped REST PUT to complete the dual identity write. On retry exhaustion, file label-only-orphan-quarantine bug and suspend the outbound for L until human review. Addresses the pre-mortem's identified dedup-JQL fossilization bug class.
- Previously mapped local jira-* whose Jira twin is absent from JQL working set: (inbound, probe) — per-issue REST GET disambiguates the 4-way fork: hard-delete, redirect (issue moved to another project, key changed), out-of-window (closed and aged out), or trash (recoverable). On hard-delete, the local content is preserved and a fresh outbound create produces a new Jira issue with a newly-minted dso-id; local renames from jira-dig-XXXX to jira-dig-YYYY (new key). Probe runs even in dry-run mode (read-only REST calls).

Applier dispatch (applier.py). Narrow function per (direction, action) pair: inbound_create, inbound_update, inbound_delete, inbound_clean_label, inbound_repair_property, inbound_probe, outbound_create, outbound_update, outbound_delete. Each leaf accepts only matching-direction mutations and raises DirectionMismatchError on wrong-direction input — turns the prior inversion bug into a type error at unit-test time. Each leaf <= 50 LOC, independently testable.

Outbound updates apply status via a local_to_jira_status mapping config. Missing-entry behavior: if a local status has no entry in the mapping table, the differ raises StatusMappingError and aborts the pass before any outbound write. Operator alert is filed naming the unmapped status; comment-fallback is reserved exclusively for the case where a mapped target status is illegal in the Jira workflow scheme — preventing the comment channel from becoming a silent sink for stale-mapping noise. On 400-from-illegal-transition (the workflow scheme rejects the mapped target state), the applier emits a Jira comment ("local status changed to X") instead of retrying. Convergent OSS pattern from espressif and canonical gh-jira-sync-bot prior art.

JQL dedup at differ time requires both identifiers: label dso-id:<L> AND entity property dso_local_id=<L> must both be present and matching for a Jira issue to count as the canonical mapping target for local L. Label-only matches trigger (inbound, repair_property) or (inbound, clean_label), never silent binding. The rollback path in outbound_create wraps client.delete_issue in _call_with_retry (same budget, same backoff as the create itself) so transient API failures cannot convert a partial identity write into permanent corruption.

Fetcher scoping (fetcher.py). JQL: project = DIG AND (resolution = Unresolved OR updated >= -1h). Closed-on-both-sides issues exit the working set entirely; reopens are caught by the 1-hour grace window (grace > 20-min cron cadence). Pagination uses startAt offset (safe at the ~2k-issue working-set ceiling; never deprecated for low totals; avoids documented nextPageToken data-loss bugs JRACLOUD-94632 and Atlassian community thread #3066609). Fallback detector: if startAt is removed in a future ACLI version, same-nextPageToken-twice triggers abort-and-alert. Silent-truncation detector: Jira Cloud has an undocumented hard ceiling of 1000 results for JQL search; if a page returns exactly 1000 results AND ACLI's total-or-isLast indicator does not strictly confirm 'less than 1000 total in working set', the fetcher aborts the pass with a BRIDGE_ALERT jql-result-truncation-suspected. This prevents the differ from treating a silently-truncated set as authoritative. The --fields parameter excludes `resolution` and `updated` (ACLI rejects these); both are used in the JQL clause only.

Invariants (invariants.py). Preserves check_at_most_one_dso_local_id. Adds check_dual_identity_complete: for every issue with a dso-id label, verify the dso_local_id entity property is present and matches; for every issue with a dso_local_id property, verify the dso-id label is present and matches. Disagreement auto-files a bug ticket via the existing anomaly path (cap 5/pass + 24h dedup). Catches Jira admin renames and partial identity writes before they cascade.

Concurrency contract. reconcile-bridge.yml uses GHA concurrency group { group: reconcile-bridge, cancel-in-progress: false } to prevent overlapping passes from GHA cron. The orchestrator additionally checks for an in-flight tickets-branch advisory lock (.reconciler-pass-lock committed at pass start, removed at pass end) before dispatching the differ. If a concurrent pass is detected, the new pass exits cleanly with a manifest entry concurrent-pass-deferred and no mutations applied. This closes the operator+cron race in Phase 3 and the two-operator race in Phase 1-2.

Rollout machinery (reconcile.py). Mode flag (dry-run | bootstrap-strict | bootstrap-throttle | live) sourced from workflow_dispatch input per invocation (no persistent state). Strict allow-list validation at orchestrator entry: the mode string is compared case-sensitively against the 4 canonical values; any other value (typo, mixed-case, missing input, leading/trailing whitespace) raises ModeValidationError before any fetcher call. Operator alert is filed and the pass aborts. No silent default fallback to live. Phase advancement is gated by a tickets-branch advisory lockfile .reconciler-phase-gate whose contents declare the maximum-allowed mode for the next pass. After each pass completes, the operator updates and commits the lockfile (e.g., bootstrap-strict to bootstrap-throttle) explicitly. The orchestrator at pass entry reads the lockfile and rejects any mode greater than the lockfile-declared ceiling — converting informal operator review into a checked-into-git approval gate. Scheduled cron stays disabled through dry-run, bootstrap-strict, bootstrap-throttle phases; re-enabled at first live invocation. Phased mutation cap:
- Phase 0 (dry-run): 1 pass; cap=0 (manifest only, zero writes). All inbound_probe REST GET calls execute (read-only). Operator reviews full manifest before approving Phase 1.
- Phase 1 (bootstrap-strict): 5 passes at cap=10 mutations/pass. Asymmetric manifest each pass (outbound totals; inbound details with full field manifest; alerts with full detail). Operator reviews each pass before approving the next. Bounded blast radius: max 10 ticket-class damage per pass; 50-ticket cumulative sample is enough to detect class-level defects with manageable rollback cost.
- Phase 2 (bootstrap-throttle): 3 passes at cap=100 mutations/pass. Asymmetric manifest plus per-pass spot-check of 10% of mutations. Cumulative 350 tickets processed by end of Phase 2 — meaningful statistical confidence that no class-level defect has surfaced.
- Phase 3 (live-uncapped): scheduled cron resumes. Manifest logs to GHA workflow log only. Operator alerted only via anomaly bug tickets (cap 5/pass + 24h dedup).

Cap-overflow behavior: when derived mutation count exceeds cap, apply mutations up to cap in deterministic order (sorted by tuple (direction, action, jira_key or local_id)) then log deferred mutations to manifest. Next pass re-derives from current state (stateless), so the deferred set may shift if underlying state changed between passes — operator review of the deferred-list delta is the trust signal that progress is real. Convergence may take more passes when churn is high.

Asymmetric manifest renderer: during dry-run plus bootstrap-strict, outbound emits totals (counts of creates/updates/deletes); inbound emits per-ticket detail (full field manifest so erroneous Jira data is catchable). During bootstrap-throttle, both directions emit summary plus operator-spot-check sample. During live, GHA workflow log only; operator attention only via anomaly path.

Conflict policy (preserved). Local wins on state (status, assignee, priority, type, title, description, deletions). Additive merge inbound for set-valued fields (comments, watchers, labels, links) with per-element provenance (origin: local | jira). Attachments explicitly out of scope (no-op in inbound_create and outbound_create).

Identity model (preserved, verified at ACLI layer). Every outbound_create writes both label dso-id:<uuid> and entity property dso_local_id with mandatory-or-alert discipline. Search-by-identity uses label JQL as primary; per-issue REST property read is confirmation/audit. JQL on entity properties is not supported on Jira Cloud (verified during prior epic).

Modules deleted by this epic: bootstrap.py, orphan_band.py, duplicates_band.py, stale_band.py, open_count_skew_band.py (banded-bootstrap construct retired; derivable design treats every pass identically). All bridge_state/ write paths removed. All mapping.json write paths removed; reads removed.

Modules preserved: conflict_resolver.py (still applies), alert_store.py (BRIDGE_ALERT sink), health.py (per-pass health record), capability_check.py, _concurrency.py, _attestation.py. ACLI layer unchanged (36 contract tests plus 4 bug fixes shipped on main from prior epic).

Out of scope. Attachment sync (binary handling, documented as explicit no-op). Project-key reuse handling (single-project usage; not relevant until DIG is renamed or recreated). Webhook fan-in (pull-only design avoids webhook-ordering footguns).

## Success Criteria

1. Direction safety: zero new duplicate Jira issues created across all reconciler passes in this epic. Verify by ACLI JQL `project = DIG AND labels NOT LIKE "dso-id-*" AND status != Closed AND created >= <epic-start-ts>` cross-referenced against `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --status=open` filtered to jira-* IDs; assert zero mismatches.

2. Stateless convergence: 2 consecutive workflow_dispatch runs on unchanged (local, Jira) state produce byte-identical mutation manifests under canonical serialization. Manifest serialization MUST use json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2) with mutation list pre-sorted by tuple (direction, action, jira_key or local_id) and per-mutation field dicts also sorted by key. Byte-equality is asserted on this canonical form, not arbitrary Python dict-insertion-order output. Verify by triggering reconcile-bridge.yml twice back-to-back on converged state; diff the manifests; assert mutation list identical and byte-equal.

3. Pagination stability: pass against a working set with simulated mid-fetch update emits exactly one mutation per affected issue. Verify by inserting a marker update on a throwaway DIG issue immediately after pass-start; assert manifest contains exactly one mutation referencing that issue.

4. Disappeared-from-Jira fork: for each of {hard-delete, trash-and-restore, project-move, out-of-window}, the appropriate branch fires with correct outcome. Verify by per-branch throwaway-issue test executing the disambiguation; assert correct behavior per branch (hard-delete creates new Jira with fresh dso-id; redirect updates local mapping to new key; trash-and-restore no-op; out-of-window silent exclusion).

5. Status-taxonomy fallback: workflow-illegal local-to-Jira status push produces a Jira comment, not a 400 retry storm. Verify by picking a Jira issue in a status from which `Done` is illegal in the workflow scheme; trigger a local status change to a state that maps to `Done`; assert the next reconciler pass emits a Jira comment containing `local status changed to <X>` and zero update_issue 400 errors in pass health record.

6. Schema-drift anomaly: removing dso_local_id property from a managed Jira issue triggers check_dual_identity_complete to file a bug ticket within the same pass. Verify by REST-DELETE the property on a throwaway managed DIG issue; trigger workflow_dispatch; assert bug ticket appears within the same pass tagged with appropriate dedup_key.

7. Dedup-fossilization defense: a label-only orphan (Jira issue with dso-id label but missing dso_local_id property) claiming an active local id does NOT bind via JQL dedup; the differ emits (inbound, repair_property) on first encounter and quarantines if repair fails. Verify by manually constructing the failure state (write dso-id label without entity property to a throwaway DIG issue claiming an active local id); assert the next pass emits inbound_repair_property and that the local outbound for that id is suspended pending property write success or operator intervention.

8. Stale-label cleanup: the 197 bridge orphans visible at epic start (Jira issues with dso-id labels pointing to nonexistent local ids) resolve via inbound_clean_label across the first 5 capped passes. Verify by capturing bridge-fsck label-only-orphan count BEFORE Phase 1 and AFTER Phase 2 completes; assert count drops to 0.

9. Synthetic drift heals: existing tests/drift_injection/inject-and-heal.sh against live DIG with all 3 modes (orphan, mislabel, missing-prop) — each mode heals within 1 pass and bridge-fsck exits 0. Verify by harness returns exit 0 for all 3 modes in sequence with no operator intervention.

10. Steady-state convergence: 5 consecutive workflow_dispatch runs in Phase 3 (live-uncapped) on converged state exit 0 with <= 5 mutations per pass. Verify after anomaly heal SCs pass; run 5 sequential workflow_dispatch in mode=live; assert each run's mutation_count <= 5 and exit code 0.


11. Per-element-class round-trip idempotency, LIVE VERIFIED. For each syncable data element class — scalar (title, description, status, priority, type, assignee) and collection-with-provenance (comments, labels excluding dso-id, watchers, links) — exercise the create/edit/delete path bidirectionally and assert exactly-one application per pass with zero duplicate generation across 3 consecutive passes after the initial sync. Test matrix (executable in-session against throwaway DIG issues + local tickets): (a) inbound-comment-create: add a Jira comment; pass 1 mirrors into local; passes 2-3 emit zero mutations referencing that comment. (b) outbound-comment-create: add a local comment; pass 1 mirrors to Jira; passes 2-3 emit zero mutations. (c) comment-edit bidirectional: edit on each side; verify local-wins behavior plus zero re-application. (d) comment-delete: bidirectional, verify provenance-aware behavior (Jira-origin element removal does not auto-propagate to local; local-origin removal propagates). (e) label-create/edit/delete bidirectional (excluding the reconciler-owned dso-id label). (f) link-create/edit/delete bidirectional. Assert across 3 consecutive passes after any single element operation, the manifest mutation count for that element class is exactly 1 then 0 then 0.

12. No-duplicate-element invariant across full bootstrap, LIVE VERIFIED. After Phase 1 plus Phase 2 completion (350 cumulative tickets processed), for every synced ticket pair (local id and its mapped Jira key) assert: comments_in_jira count == comments_in_local count; labels_in_jira count (excluding dso-id) == labels_in_local count; links_in_jira count == links_in_local count. Any mismatch indicates duplicate generation by the differ. Verify by bulk readout across the post-Phase-2 mapped set; assert zero count mismatches.


## Scenario Analysis

The canonical scrutiny pipeline (Red Team plus Blue Team) surfaced 22 surviving failure scenarios after filtering. Critical and several high-severity scenarios are addressed by inline spec amendments above; the remaining are documented here as accepted risks with mitigation notes.

Addressed by inline amendments above:
- Concurrent workflow_dispatch race (critical) — concurrency contract (GHA group + advisory lockfile)
- ACLI 1000-result silent truncation (critical) — silent-truncation detector in fetcher
- RECONCILER_MODE input validation gap (critical) — strict allow-list validation at orchestrator entry
- Bootstrap module deletion breaks remaining imports (high) — no-remaining-imports closure check
- local_to_jira_status missing-entry silently falls through (high) — StatusMappingError on missing entry
- Byte-identical mutation lists across passes (high) — canonical serialization spec in SC2
- Phase boundary approval is informal (high) — .reconciler-phase-gate lockfile

Accepted risks with documented mitigation:

- Pagination drift under steady DIG churn (runtime, high): Issues updated during pagination can shift between pages, causing duplicate or omitted mutations. Mitigation: the anomaly path catches the persistent corruption signature; oscillating mutations across passes are visible in per-pass manifest diff at SC2 verification time.

- Local state read non-atomic w.r.t. in-flight ticket transitions (runtime, high): While a pass runs, parallel sessions may transition/create/close tickets. Mitigation: outbound write attempts include a pre-write recheck against the snapshot source state; mismatches abort the individual mutation with a local-state-changed-mid-pass alert; the next pass re-derives.

- Inbound probe REST GET storm during dry-run (runtime, high): Phase 0 dry-run runs inbound_probe REST GETs for every previously mapped jira-* whose twin is absent; could trigger Jira rate limits. Mitigation: cap inbound_probe at 50 REST GETs per pass during dry-run; deferred probes log to manifest with probe-deferred-rate-limit annotation; next pass picks up the remainder.

- Cap-overflow ordering — non-monotonic progress under churn (runtime, high): Deferred mutations re-derive each pass; underlying state changes can shift the deferred set. Mitigation: spec defines deterministic ordering (direction, action, jira_key or local_id) for cap-overflow; the deferred-list delta between passes is itself an operator-visible signal.

- GHA 6-hour timeout vs uncapped Phase 3 pass (runtime, high): A bulk Jira admin operation producing 100K issues in the updated-1h window could kill the pass mid-apply. Mitigation: reconcile.py emits a pass-duration alert if elapsed time exceeds 4 hours mid-apply; partial-write state is auto-detected by check_dual_identity_complete on the next pass.

- Phase 2 to 3 cron-enable race (deployment, high): If operator merges the cron-enable PR while a Phase 2 workflow_dispatch pass is still running, the next cron tick could fire mid-pass. Mitigation: the .reconciler-phase-gate lockfile means the cron tick reads the lockfile and refuses to advance past bootstrap-throttle until the operator commits the lockfile update to live.

- ACLI binary version drift local vs GHA runner (deployment, high): GHA runner may install a different ACLI version. Mitigation: reconcile-bridge.yml pins ACLI to a specific version via the install step; the 36 contract tests are tagged with the pinned version. Closure check verifies the pin is present in the workflow yml.

- JIRA_API_TOKEN rotation mid-rollout (deployment, high): Token rotation between passes invalidates auth and could leave partial identity writes. Mitigation: 401 response triggers fatal pass abort; operator alert escalates to P1 bug filing via the anomaly path; the rollback retry wrapper is bounded by the 200-call REST budget.

- Anomaly cap 5/pass + 24h dedup suppresses signal during outbreak (configuration, high): A 200-issue bulk anomaly burns the budget on the first 5; remaining silently suppressed. Mitigation: introduce a same-class-anomaly-burst-detected meta-alert that fires when a class hits the cap; this single meta-alert summarizes the burst rather than enumerating each.

- Atomic snapshot pair assumption (assumption, high): The differ assumes (local, jira_state) is read as a consistent pair, but Jira fetch is network-bound and slow. Mitigation: SC2 byte-identical verification is performed with both passes triggered back-to-back on enforced quiescence; the assumption is documented and the eventually-consistent failure mode is explicitly acceptable.

- Probe REST GET disappeared-key response pattern stability (assumption, high): Jira Cloud trash/redirect/404 semantics have changed historically. Mitigation: SC4 verification is re-runnable at any time against live Jira; if Atlassian changes trash semantics, the test catches the misclassification.

- Operator can rollback Phase 1 within hours (assumption, high): No explicit rollback playbook exists for Phase 1 damage. Mitigation: a dedicated rollback script plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/rollback-phase-1.sh is included as a Closure Check artifact; the script bulk-strips dso-id labels added during a specified time window and deletes any local jira-* tickets created within the same window.

- No Jira admin schema-level operations during rollout (assumption, medium): Bulk admin operations between passes could produce 100s of repair_property mutations exceeding cap=100 in Phase 2. Mitigation: operator policy — coordinate with Jira admin to defer schema-level operations during the rollout window. Documented in the runbook.

- Closed-on-both-sides reopens always touch updated field (assumption, medium): Rare Jira automation rules can flip status without touching updated. Mitigation: the weekly fsck audit (CC4, carried forward from 3a03) catches drift that escapes the 1-hour grace window.

## Closure Checks

bridge_state/ directory NOT present on tickets branch. Verify by `git ls-tree tickets bridge_state/` returns no entries.

mapping.json NOT present on tickets branch. Verify by `git ls-tree tickets bridge_state/mapping.json` returns nothing.

differ.py, applier.py, fetcher.py, reconcile.py updated per Approach; banded-bootstrap modules deleted AND no remaining imports of those modules anywhere in the repo (grep -rEn 'from dso_reconciler.(bootstrap|orphan_band|duplicates_band|stale_band|open_count_skew_band)|import .*dso_reconciler.(bootstrap|orphan_band|duplicates_band|stale_band|open_count_skew_band)' plugins/ tests/ .github/ .claude/ returns zero matches — prevents post-deploy ImportError where a script outside dso_reconciler/ still references a deleted band module). Verify by `git ls-tree origin/main plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/{bootstrap,orphan_band,duplicates_band,stale_band,open_count_skew_band}.py` returns no entries.

local_to_jira_status config table present and consumed by outbound_update. Verify by grep for the symbol; unit test confirms 400-on-illegal-transition triggers comment-fallback branch.

check_dual_identity_complete invariant present in invariants.py and wired into per-pass invariant scan. Unit test confirms label-without-property and property-without-label both trigger bug-file path.

inbound_clean_label, inbound_repair_property, inbound_probe dispatch leaves present in applier.py with DirectionMismatchError guards. Unit tests confirm direction-mismatch raises.

Rollback delete_issue in outbound_create wrapped in _call_with_retry. Unit test confirms transient failure on rollback triggers retry then BRIDGE_ALERT (not silent corruption).

JQL dedup at differ time requires both identifiers (label AND entity property). Unit test confirms label-only matches do NOT bind via dedup.

Rollout mode flag (workflow_dispatch input) honored by reconcile.py for dry-run / bootstrap-strict / bootstrap-throttle / live. Unit test confirms dry-run pass writes manifest with zero ACLI writes (mocked AcliClient assertion); bootstrap-strict pass aborts cleanly when mutation count exceeds cap=10 (deferred mutations recorded).

reconcile-bridge.yml scheduled cron disabled through Phase 0-1-2; re-enabled at Phase 3 boundary. Verify by workflow `state` transition committed to main (visible in .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml diff).

All 10 Success Criteria verified in-session against live origin/main + live DIG Jira (per in-session verification protocol established in prior epic, preserved here).

- Per-element provenance tracking present in conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES for set-valued fields (comments, labels, watchers, links). Verified live against a throwaway DIG issue plus its local mirror: add a comment via the Jira API; run pass 1 and confirm inbound_update produces exactly one mutation that adds the comment to the local mirror; run passes 2 and 3 and confirm zero mutations reference that comment. Repeat for labels, watchers, links. This is the load-bearing mechanism backing SC11 and SC12; the assertion is on live Jira plus live local tracker state, not on unit-test fixtures.

- Live bidirectional field-class disposition validation covers all 6 cases per (direction × action) combination for each FIELD_CLASS entry: scalar-divergence (local-wins), additive-collection-add (provenance-aware merge), additive-collection-remove (origin-aware: local-origin removal propagates outbound; Jira-origin removal stays local-preserved per the additive policy). Each case is exercised against a real throwaway DIG issue plus a real local ticket pair; the assertion is that the third consecutive pass on the converged state produces zero mutations for that field class. Live verification, not mocked. Test harness lives at tests/integration/test-derivable-bidirectional-field-classes.sh (new test file; pattern follows the existing 36-pattern ACLI contract harness at tests/scripts/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py).

Carried forward from prior epic 3a03 as preconditions, no re-verification needed:
- CC1 legacy bridge-outbound.yml and inbound-bridge.yml deleted from .github/workflows/. VERIFIED in 3a03 PR #327.
- CC3b out-of-band heartbeat canary firing on simulated disable. VERIFIED in 3a03 story 7004 closure.
- CC4 weekly-bridge-fsck.yml runs end-to-end with stable snapshot. VERIFIED in 3a03 via 2 consecutive on-demand runs returning identical anomaly counts.
- CC5 no legacy bridge code refs remain. VERIFIED in 3a03 PR #334.
- CC7 rollback-impossible-after-Nh forward-fix path documented in rollback-bridge-cutover.sh header. VERIFIED in 3a03 commit ed41294987.
- SC7 (rollback dry-run) VERIFIED in 3a03 story 7339 user-override.

## State Lifecycle

| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| imported:reconciler-bootstrap tag (per local ticket) | applier.inbound_create | never (additive only) | operator triage (manual ticket filtering) | never retired (durable audit marker for the bootstrap import set) |
| dso-id:<uuid> Jira label (per issue) | applier.outbound_create (identity write) | never (id is immutable) | fetcher JQL dedup + differ direction derivation | applier.inbound_clean_label (only when label points to nonexistent local id) |
| dso_local_id Jira entity property (per issue) | applier.outbound_create (identity write) + applier.inbound_repair_property (when only label was set) | never (id is immutable) | invariants.check_dual_identity_complete + audit reads | never retired (durable identity) |
| RECONCILER_MODE (per pass) | workflow_dispatch operator input | per-invocation | reconcile_once mode dispatch + manifest renderer | per-pass; not persisted |

## External Dependencies

DIG Jira project (read+write, label + entity-property API): ownership exists, handling claude_auto, claude_has_access yes. ACLI + JIRA_API_TOKEN verified in 3a03 (36 contract tests on main).

GitHub Actions runner for reconcile-bridge.yml: ownership exists, handling claude_auto, claude_has_access yes.

External heartbeat monitor: ownership user_setup_required (configured in 3a03 story 7004), handling user_manual, already working. Carries forward.

## Dependencies

None. This epic depends only on what is already shipped on origin/main post-3a03 cleanup.
